```{r setup-mascot_studio, include = FALSE, echo = FALSE}
studio_character <- if (exists("studio_character")) studio_character else formals(mascot::mascot)$character
```

```{r mascot_studio-try-live, echo = FALSE}
if (!in_studio()) guide_try_live("mascot_studio")
```

### Open a useful starting point

Launch the studio from an interactive R console:

```r
mascot::mascot_studio()
mascot::mascot_studio(fn = "mascot_theme")
```

Use `fn` without parentheses to start on a particular function's Guide.
Leaving it at `NULL` opens `mascot_mood`. Choose a character with `character`:

```{r mascot_studio-character-call, echo = FALSE}
htmltools::tags$pre(htmltools::tags$code(paste0(
  'mascot::mascot_studio(character = "', studio_character, '")'
)))
```

### Three views, one app

| `view` | Starting point |
|--------|----------------|
| `"studio"` | The studio: every function, with a live mascot and controls. |
| `"examples"` | The bundled example gallery, with source code and launch calls. |
| `"theme"` | Theme a mascot: a palette, your own colours or your brand's for one character, with the code to copy. |

```r
mascot::mascot_studio(view = "examples")
mascot::mascot_studio(view = "theme")
```

The studio and examples views share one interface. The view chooses what it shows
first; `fn` chooses the Guide function in the studio view. Choose "Preview page"
under "Host mode" to compare moods and sizes as `mascot_preview()` draws them.
The theme view is a page of its own, also opened by `mascot_example("theme")` and
from the studio's More menu.

### Inspect without launching

```r
app <- mascot::mascot_studio(fn = "mascot_theme", run = FALSE)
inherits(app, "shiny.appobj")
```

This returns `TRUE`: `run = FALSE` gives you an app object rather than opening
a server. By contrast, `mascot_example(..., run = FALSE)` gives a file path.

### What to look at first

Start with a mood change and its status text. Then compare a palette in light
and dark modes, and try the motion switches. Use the Guide for worked explanations,
Help for the function reference, and the generated code when adapting a choice
to your own app.

The studio works offline with mascot, Shiny and the optional packages bslib and
knitr available locally. Its interface is experimental, so revisit the generated
code when upgrading.

```{r mascot_studio-mistakes, echo = FALSE}
if (!in_studio()) guide_mistakes_html("mascot_studio", studio_character)
```
